name: Lumos LUS2
summary:
Lumos LUS2 is a full-size bipedal humanoid for research, education and commercial demonstrations. Its modular, open architecture combines natural straight-leg walking with articulated arms, environmental perception and support for secondary development. Lumos identifies navigation, object handling and human-robot interaction as intended areas of use.

The manufacturer lists a height of 1.60 metres, weight of 57 kg and 28 joint-module degrees of freedom. Each arm has seven degrees of freedom and a stated 3 kg payload. LiDAR, binocular depth sensing and an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin computer support

Lumos LUS2 is a full-size bipedal humanoid for research, education and commercial demonstrations. Its modular, open architecture combines natural straight-leg walking with articulated arms, environmental perception and support for secondary development. Lumos identifies navigation, object handling and human-robot interaction as intended areas of use.

The manufacturer lists a height of 1.60 metres, weight of 57 kg and 28 joint-module degrees of freedom. Each arm has seven degrees of freedom and a stated 3 kg payload. LiDAR, binocular depth sensing and an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin computer support perception and application development; dexterous hands are configurable.
